writeup.p: S31PacketWindowProperty carries one container property update: unsigned byte windowId, short property id, short value. The meaning of the property id is container-type specific. The furnace uses 0 for burn time remaining, 1 for item cook progress, 2 for total cook time. The enchantment table uses 0-2 for the three level slots, the brewing stand 0 for brew time, the beacon 0 for power level. Tile entities push these through updateProgressBar whenever a field changes, typically once per tick while active.

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleWindowProperty resolves the container by window id and calls Container.updateProgressBar, which writes into the container's progress array. The GUI renderers (furnace flame, enchant glint, brewing bubbles) read that array every frame. Server side, EntityPlayerMP.sendProgressBarUpdate (lines 783 and 788 in the bundled sources) forwards a single property and sendAllWindowProperties pushes every field when the window opens. The values are absolute, not deltas.

None of the 8 clients has a module for this packet. The only non-vanilla hits are the Rise 6.x NetworkAPI script registration table (both 6.1.30 and 6.2.4) and the vanilla handler files. Auto-enchant and auto-brewer style modules, which would read S31 to time clicks, do not exist in these corpora. The 8 clients concentrate their inventory effort on stealing, armor handling and transaction sync, not on container progress.

There is no exploit surface in this corpus. S31 is display-only state: the client renders the value and nothing else depends on it. A malicious server could flood S31 to churn the GUI renderer, but that is a server-side attack with no client counterpart, and no anti-cheat measures the packet because it carries no movement, combat or inventory-trust signal. Modules that needed progress data would have to parse the property stream themselves; none do.

overview: The container progress packet: furnace flames, enchant levels, brewing bubbles. Zero module hits in the 8 clients; the only non-vanilla reference is the Rise 6.x script API registration table. This is render data with no cheat value in this corpus.
server_handling: EntityPlayerMP.sendProgressBarUpdate constructs S31(windowId, var, value) and sends it whenever the open container's fields change; sendAllWindowProperties (line 788) pushes every field when the window opens. NetHandlerPlayClient.handleWindowProperty calls Container.updateProgressBar on the resolved container, which stores the value for the GUI to read. No validation, no rate limit, no client echo.
protocol_notes: Wire: unsigned byte windowId, short property, short value. Property semantics are fixed per container class, not negotiated: furnace 0-2, enchantment table 0-2, brewing stand 0, beacon 0. Values are absolute ticks or levels so the GUI can render progress without keeping history. PLAY state only, and only while the corresponding container is open; the server stops sending once the player closes the window.
anticheat_landscape: Nothing to flag: S31 is server-authoritative display data, sent at most a few times per second per open container, and no movement, combat or inventory-trust check reads it. The only conceivable abuse is a server spamming S31 to load the GUI render path, a denial-of-service vector aimed at the client rather than something a cheat client would do.
general_hooks: No module hooks exist in the corpus. The packet reaches containers exclusively through the vanilla handler.
client_variations: Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 register S31 in NetworkAPI so scripts can listen to it; that registration is the only non-vanilla reference in the corpus.
